nota: Archived NASA data, downloaded on 2026-11-14. Daily dose = mean of absorbed_dose_rate from Curiosity's RAD instrument on the surface of Mars. Calm reference: 3.85 µGy/h (mean of May 18-19, 2024). Level = day mean / calm: below 1.6 = 0, below 10 = 1, below 100 = 2, otherwise 3. Night low = min_temp of the sol from Curiosity's REMS weather station; heating needs 2 batteries at -80 °C or colder, otherwise 1. Forecast range: made by the game from the DONKI events known that morning (flares, CMEs, particles, ENLIL runs); it is not an official NASA forecast.
instrumento: the RAD instrument on NASA's Curiosity rover, on the surface of Mars

fontes.nome: Curiosity RAD radiation dose, via NASA OSDR RadLab
ENLIL solar wind model runs (CME arrival at Mars), NASA DONKI

dias.curto: Welcome to Mars! A very cold night is coming.
dias.aviso: Welcome to Mars! The crew landed in Jezero crater, where the Perseverance rover works. The weather and radiation numbers come from Curiosity, in Gale Crater. Tonight will be very cold.
dias.fato: Mars air is 100 times thinner than Earth's. Nights get freezing!

dias.curto: NASA says: storm clouds reach Mars tomorrow!
dias.aviso: Alert: NASA's ENLIL model says clouds of solar material (CMEs) launched on May 16 and 17 will reach Mars tomorrow. Get ready!
dias.fato: A NASA computer model called ENLIL predicts when solar storms arrive.

dias.curto: The CMEs should hit Mars today!
dias.aviso: Alert! At 05:36 UTC a CME left the Sun at 2,678 km/s, the fastest of the month.
dias.fato: Today Curiosity measured 18 times more radiation than on a calm day!

dias.aviso: The clouds of solar material are passing by Mars.
dias.fato: On Mars, a roof of soil can block radiation.

dias.curto: The Sun looks quieter. Keep building!
dias.aviso: The Sun looks quieter. A good day to build!
dias.fato: A day on Mars is called a sol. It lasts 24 hours and 39 minutes.

dias.aviso: The Sun is quiet near Mars today. Keep building the base.
dias.fato: Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos.

dias.curto: Quiet Sun. The base is taking shape.
dias.aviso: Calm. The base is taking shape.
dias.fato: Mars air presses over 100 times less than Earth's air.

dias.aviso: Last day: the base must be finished tonight!
